then.prompt: Put a Zombie from your banished zone into your graveyard to keep Bridge of Damnation?

_comment:
'**Go again** / At the start of each turn, destroy this unless you put a zombie from your banished zone into your graveyard.'

GoAgain is an UNCONDITIONAL printed keyword here (printed_keywords; the text gates nothing on it) - it fires from the card DB keywords field and is deliberately NOT authored; authoring it again would be a defect.

TRIGGER: START_OF_EACH_TURN maps to START_OF_ANY_TURN (trigger_types.py:19), which engine.py:1475-1481 dispatches to BOTH players' zones on every turn, and _dsl_permanent_zones includes player.auras (engine.py:1456) - so this Aura hears the event on each player's turn, which is what 'each turn' means. The choice belongs to the aura's controller: ask_yes_no/_ask_player resolve cid via _controller_id(card).

UNLESS SHAPE: 'destroy this unless you put a zombie ...' is one CONDITIONAL wrapping a MAY with an else block, not two effects with inverted conditions (there is nothing to invert against - DSL_REFERENCE 'unless'). The outer CONDITIONAL is load-bearing, not decoration: gated on CARD_IN_ZONE{zone banished, subtypes [Zombie]} it distinguishes the two printed cases. With no Zombie in the banished zone there is nothing to put, so the else destroys this - if the gate were instead hung on the MAY itself, the loader would pop it into an effect-level gate that skips the WHOLE MAY including its else (effect_types.py:3794-3798), and the aura would survive a turn it should not. With a Zombie present, MAY offers the move; declining runs its else destroy. MOVE_MATCHING takes the canonical object target spec (effect_types.py:3593-3612): zone BANISHED resolves through _object_zone_cards, the SUBTYPE_IN filter is evaluated per candidate card, amount 1 prompts the controller to choose which Zombie (_ask_player), and put_object routes it to the graveyard. DESTROY_SELF with no filters hits the bare branch that calls canonical destroy() on the source card from whatever zone it sits in (effect_types.py:2494-2498).
